To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glycerol-extracting Paramecium reversibly reverses the orientation of its cilia when exposed to a solution containing ATP, calcium, or zinc.
the predominant orientation of ciliary beat in glycerol extracted Paramecium can be changed to an anterior orientation by a combination of ATP, calcium and zinc.

the predominant orientation of ciliated Paramecium in glycerol is toward the posterior, that this orientation is reversed toward the anterior when the cell is exposed to a mixture of calcium, ATP, and zinc, and that the degree of reorientation is graded as a function the concentration of each factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of the orientation of the cilia of Paramecium.
the control of the orientation of cilia.
the control of ciliary orientation in Paramecium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reorientation of the glycerol-extract cilia in the presence of the three factors is the result of a calcium-induced ciliary reversal.
ATP, calcium, zinc, and possibly magnesium ions are essential for the control of ciliary reversal in Paramecium.
the cilia in extracted Paramecium respond to ATP, calcium, zinc, and the pH of the medium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ciliary reversal is initiated by calcium which is displaced from an exchanger system by ATP and zinc.
cilia in glycol-extracted Paramecia respond to a mixture of zinc and calcium ions in the presence of ATP.
the cilia are oriented toward the posterior by an unknown mechanism which involves the binding of zinc ions to an exchanger system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
zinc ions are essential to the ciliary response to calcium.
the cilia in Paramecium can respond to ATP, Ca2+, and Zn2+ and that these ciliary responses are mediated through a cation exchanger.
the orientation of Paramecium cilia can be controlled by ATP, calcium, zinc, and other factors.
